title.narrative: Education of asylum seeker, Ukrainian and Afghan children arriving in England

description.narrative: The Department for Education activity is an estimate of the department’s annual spend on the education of asylum seeker and Ukrainian children who are of compulsory school age in England – i.e. of primary and secondary ages – for the first 12 months after their asylum application is lodged or they arrived in the UK. It is important to note that there is not a specific budget for this spend. The DfE provides funding to schools in England (via local authorities in the case of maintained schools) through the national funding formula and various other grants, including the pupil premium grant, worth a total of over £55bn per year. The DfE makes an estimate of how much of this total is, in effect, allocated to schools’ budgets due to asylum seeker, Ukrainian and Afghan children in their first 12 months in the country being on roll. All pupils on roll at a school attract funding to their school in the same way, irrespective of whether or not they are asylum seeker children or Ukrainian arrivals or Afghan arrivals. In 2023, the Department for Education also provided bespoke funding to support children who arrived in the UK through two migration schemes: Homes for Ukraine and the Afghan Citizens Resettlement Scheme. All the spending being estimated takes place domestically in the UK.

This is set out in the department’s ODA spending statement: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/official-development-assistance-dfe-spending-statement/official-development-assistance-oda-dfe-spending-statement.

recipient-country.narrative: The UK has been recorded in the country code in the absence of being able to select a suitable alternative option. The recipient countries are developing countries unspecified, although the people in receipt of the ODA spending are here in the UK.
